entries.title: Kaysender Origin System
entries.summary: A Hypertext d20-compatible character-creation layer that converts Kaysender backgrounds into origins without replacing ancestry or class.
body: An origin records the work, community, danger, or social position that shaped a character before 1st level. It sits alongside ancestry and class: ancestry describes inherited or cultural traits, class governs adventuring progression, and origin supplies a modest package of trained skills, practical knowledge, starting equipment, and social access.

Choose one origin at character creation. An origin does not consume a feat and does not grant extra class levels. A campaign may allow a player to write a new origin by following the same limits: two associated skills, one focused +2 origin bonus, one trade or professional specialty, one modest equipment package, and one narrative access feature that creates opportunities rather than automatic success.

Origin benefits use established Hypertext d20 structures. Skill access adds named skills to the character's class-skill list at 1st level. An origin bonus is an untyped bonus tied narrowly to the origin's field and should not replace a full skill investment. Contacts, safe harbor, workshop access, or audiences remain subject to local law, reputation, cost, and roleplaying.

sections.heading: Standard origin package
body: Associated skills: The two listed skills are always class skills for the character. If both were already class skills, choose one additional thematically related class skill with GM approval.

Origin focus: Gain the listed +2 origin bonus on the narrow checks described by the origin. This bonus represents lived familiarity and does not stack with another origin bonus applying to the same check.

Trade specialty: Gain literacy in the normal languages used by the origin's community and familiarity with the listed Craft, Profession, or tool-equivalent specialty. The character may buy ranks in that skill normally.
Starting package: Add the listed practical gear to normal class starting equipment. Currency values are deliberately modest and may be exchanged for campaign-equivalent supplies.

Access feature: The character knows how to request aid, information, shelter, or professional access from the relevant community. The feature opens a negotiation; it never compels an NPC, erases a debt, or overrides law.

sections.heading: Combining origins with classes
body: Airship Engineer commonly pairs with Guild Apprentice, Guild Artisan of the Sky Trade, Sky Reclaimer, or Skyfarer.
Air Captain commonly pairs with Skyfarer, Pirate, Skybound Noble, or Sky Reclaimer.
Sky Warden commonly pairs with Abyss Watcher, Driftlander, Homesteader, or Skyfarer.
Any standard Hypertext d20-compatible class can select any origin. The pairings above are setting guidance, not prerequisites.
